items.informal_name: Sigma product of intervals [1, N] over [m, M]
items.type: ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Finset ((n : ℕ) × (Fin n → ℕ))
items.informal_description: The finite set formed by taking the dependent sum over the closed interval [m, M], where each element n in this interval is associated with the product of the interval [1, N] taken n times. Each element of the resulting set is a pair (n, f), where n ranges from m to M and f is a function from Fin n to [1, N], representing an n-tuple of integers between 1 and N.
The finite set of all functions from $\{0, 1, \ldots, n-1\}$ to $\{0, 1, \ldots, d-1\}$, i.e., the set of $n$-tuples where each coordinate is an integer between $0$ and $d-1$.

items.informal_name: Compositions with bounded length and parts
items.type: ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Set ((n : ℕ) × Composition n)
items.informal_description: The set of compositions of natural numbers where the number of parts is at least $ m $ and less than $ M $, and each part is strictly less than $ N $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Sum Homomorphism for Finite Support Functions
items.type: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} [Finite σ] (w : σ → ℕ), (∀ (x : σ), w x ≠ 0) → ∀ (n : ℕ), {d | (Finsupp.weight w) d ≤ n}.Finite
items.informal_description: The additive homomorphism from the space of finite support functions $ \sigma \to_0 R $ to the module $ M $ maps each function $ d $ to the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} d(i) \cdot v_i $, where $ v_i $ denotes the vector associated with index $ i $. This homomorphism preserves addition and is defined using a fixed family of vectors $ \{v_i\}_{i \in \sigma} $.

items.informal_name: Interval between dependent finite support functions
items.type:
{ι : Type u_1} →
  {α : ι → Type u_2} →
    [inst : (i : ι) → Zero (α i)] →
      [inst_1 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (α i)] →
        [(i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (α i)] → (Π₀ (i : ι), α i) → (Π₀ (i : ι), α i) → Π₀ (i : ι), Finset (α i)
items.informal_description: For dependent finite support functions $f$ and $g$ with values in a family of locally finite ordered types $\alpha_i$, this function returns the dependent finite support function whose value at each index $i$ is the closed interval $[f(i), g(i)]$ in $\alpha_i$. The support of the resulting function is contained in the union of the supports of $f$ and $g$, ensuring finite support since both $f$ and $g$ have finite support.
